stop_condition: Each of the six r3 findings is ruled on against the shipped artifact by the mechanism its resolution record claims, with an executed negative control wherever the claim is behavioural; the timed_out asymmetry is checked at EVERY surface that carries the claim; and no critical or high finding remains in green_check_run, the green-check envelope, or the agent-facing contract.

findings.evidence: MEASURED FALSIFICATION of the shipped clause. Drove the VERBATIM-EXTRACTED shipped green_check_run (awk 'NR>=13291 && NR<=13444') under bash 3.2.57(1)-release, against a PATH shim implementing GNU timeout's one observable contract that green_check_run reads (exit 124 on deadline, propagate otherwise). Shim sanity-checked four ways first: deadline-fire->124, self-124->124, self-3->3, green->0. Seven cases, each run once, all reproducible: (A) cap=3 over 'sleep 20', elapsed=3 -> '124 timeout true' CORRECT. (B) cap=20 over 'exit 124', elapsed=0 -> '124 timeout false' CORRECT, this is the discrimination the fix claims. (C) cap=3 over 'sleep 2; exit 124', elapsed=2 -> '124 timeout TRUE' -- FALSE POSITIVE: the deadline did NOT end the run and timed_out is true. (D) cap=3 over 'sleep 1; exit 124', elapsed=1 -> '124 timeout false' CORRECT. (E) control cap=3 over 'true' -> '0 timeout false'. (F) control cap=3 over 'false' -> '1 timeout false'. (G) cap=3 over 'sleep 3; exit 124', elapsed=3 -> '124 timeout TRUE', the irreducible case any elapsed heuristic has. Case C is the one the -1 tolerance purchases (see R4-F3). Surface enumeration: grep -rn timed_out docs/ .claude/agents/ .claude/rubrics/ returns nothing but the r3 artifact itself, so the four surfaces inside qa-gate.sh are the complete set. Rendered the shipped text with `bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh --help | nl -ba | sed -n '612,632p'` to confirm reachability and exact wording.
findings.description: THE AGENT-FACING CONTRACT STILL ASSERTS A PROPERTY THE CODE DOES NOT HAVE, in weaker form. Shipped at --help line 623: 'The separate `timed_out` boolean answers that: true ONLY when the deadline itself ended the run (the watchdog's own marker file on the fallback path; rc=124 together with elapsed wall time at or past the cap on the timeout/gtimeout path).' Case C falsifies the main clause. THE IMPLEMENTER'S OWN CODE SAYS THE OPPOSITE OF ITS OWN --help: green_check_run's header (:13323-13327) says 'on the timeout/gtimeout path it is a best-effort elapsed-time heuristic, NOT airtight the same way', and the region header (:13209-13211) names case G explicitly as a false positive. So the asymmetry was known, written down TWICE, and then not carried to the one surface an implementer agent actually reads. The trailing sentence 'A command that calls exit 124 on its own, WELL INSIDE the cap, reports timed_out=false' is phrased as reassurance, not caveat -- a reader does not infer 'therefore near the cap it reports true'. This is round 4 of this defect class at this same surface (rubric -> --help -> code header -> --help again). WHAT VERIFIES, STATED FAIRLY: the watchdog half is genuinely airtight and I confirmed its load-bearing premise by measurement under bash rather than accepting it -- kill -TERM yields wait status 143, kill -KILL yields 137, and a self-inflicted `exit 124` yields 124, so the marker file really is the only route to a forced 124 on that path. DIRECTION OF HARM, SCOPED HONESTLY: this is the MILDER direction. result=red either way, so the cannot_start_from_green refusal is unchanged; the damage is a wrong diagnosis (agent believes the cap fired and raises the cap or retries, when the suite really exited 124 on its own). Reachable for any consumer project whose test command is itself timeout-wrapped -- common, and precisely the shape green-check exists for. NOT reachable through this repo's own run-tests.sh, which uses a TIMEOUT_MARKER and never exits 124 (grep -n 'exit 124' returns nothing there). BINDING REPAIR -- ONE CLAUSE CARRYING THE SPLIT, not a softening: replace 'true only when the deadline itself ended the run' with, e.g., 'true when the deadline ended the run. This is exact on the watchdog path (the marker file). On the timeout/gtimeout path it is an INFERENCE from rc=124 plus elapsed wall time, so a command that runs to the cap and then exits 124 on its own reads as a false positive.' Narrowing or softening the wording while leaving an absolute standing would be the same defect a fifth time.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/green-check.test.sh:314 and :373 (two complementary host guards); .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh EXPECTED_SPECS comment block
findings.evidence: This finding was uncovered BY MY OWN RETRACTION (see below) and is measured twice. Host: `command -v timeout` ABSENT and `command -v gtimeout` ABSENT, bash 3.2.57(1)-release, Darwin 25.6.0. green_check_run has two implementations of timed_out: the elapsed heuristic at :13333-13358 and the marker watchdog at :13360-13443. THE SPEC HAS TWO HOST GUARDS, NOT ONE, AND THEY ARE COMPLEMENTARY: `grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*if .*command -v (g)?timeout'` returns :314 `if command -v timeout` (gating 8.6, runs ONLY WITH the binary) and :373 `if ! command -v timeout && ! command -v gtimeout` (gating 10.1b, runs ONLY WITHOUT). Exactly one fires per host. MEASURED RUNTIME COUNT, twice, by two independent instruments: (1) I ran the spec with an INERT bd stub on PATH so every assert_* still emits its PASS/FAIL line while touching no store -- 'Total: 88  Passed: 12  Failed: 76', and 88 under `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(PASS|FAIL):'`, run-tests.sh's own instrument; diffing executed names against the 89 static call sites isolated the single absentee as 8.6. (2) THE COORDINATOR'S OWN TIER, real bd, same host, later confirmed '--- green-check.test.sh: PASSED (88 assertion(s) in 69s) ---' and 'Total: 88  Passed: 88  Failed: 0'. PREDICTION STATED IN ADVANCE AND MET: before that tier reached the spec, I wrote in my round-4 report 'When your tier reaches it, it should read 88.' It read 88. The prediction is the evidence here, not the number -- a count derived from a model of the guards, stated before the confirming run, and matched.
findings.description: NO SINGLE HOST EVER TESTS BOTH ARMS OF green_check_run, AND THE ASSERTION COUNT HIDES IT. On this box every one of the 88 assertions ran the WATCHDOG arm; lines 13340 and 13353 -- the elapsed heuristic -- executed ZERO times. Every measurement in the R3-F1 resolution record ('88/88 assertions exit 0') was taken here. The arm R4-F1's false claim is ABOUT has never been executed by anyone in this repo. And because the guards are complementary the situation is symmetric: on a host WITH timeout, 10.1b is skipped and the WATCHDOG arm goes untested instead. BOTH HOSTS EMIT 88 -- an identical count over DIFFERENT CODE, which is the most misleading possible shape for a figure: it looks host-independent and is not. THIS IS THE CAUSE OF R4-F1, NOT A SEPARATE DEFECT. The overclaim survived into shipped text precisely because nothing ever ran the arm the overclaim is false about. By this change set's OWN citation -- LESSONS.md:282, 'a measurement that did not happen looking identical to one that passed' -- an arm with zero executed assertions reported inside '88/88 exit 0' is exactly that shape. CLAUDE.md's pairing rule ('at least one leg must observe the shipped artifact RUNNING') is unmet for the heuristic arm here. ON THE COORDINATOR'S QUESTION, ANSWERED AGAINST ITS OWN FRAMING: the question offered 'if a boundary test would be inherently flaky, say so -- a flaky test is not obviously better than an argued claim.' The premise does not hold. A boundary test here is NOT inherently flaky and the honest alternative is not to argue it: a `timeout` shim on PATH made it deterministic in minutes, and the fixture ALREADY prepends $FIXTURE/bin for its own bd shim, so this is a ~20-line addition in an established in-file pattern, not a new mechanism. All seven cases in R4-F1's evidence ran once each with no timing race. BINDING REPAIR, BOTH HALVES: (1) add the PATH shim so BOTH arms run on EVERY host -- fixing only the --help text in R4-F1 is not the fix, because the next wrong claim about this arm would again ship unobserved; and (2) the count in run-tests.sh must say WHICH ARM it covered, since 88 is currently silent about the one variable that changes what it measures. A shim leg that DOCUMENTS case C as a known false positive is acceptable; a shim leg that pretends it does not exist is not.

findings.evidence: The shipped predicate is `[ "$_gc_elapsed" -ge $((GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S - 1)) ]`, justified in two comments as 'a 1s tolerance for `date +%s` truncation'. THE PREMISE IS FALSE, proved two ways. ANALYTICALLY: with integer cap and real duration d >= cap, measured elapsed = floor(f+d) - 0 >= floor(d) >= cap for any start-fraction f in [0,1), so a genuine cap fire ALWAYS measures at or above the cap and truncation cannot produce an undercount. EMPIRICALLY: 120 trials of `s=$(date +%s); sleep 1; e=$(date +%s)` gave 119 x 1 and 1 x 2 -- ZERO undercounts. Corroborated by the shim runs in R4-F1: case A measured elapsed=3 at cap=3, case G measured elapsed=3 at cap=3. Neither ever came in below the cap.
findings.description: THE TOLERANCE BUYS NOTHING IN THE DIRECTION IT CLAIMS TO PROTECT, AND COSTS ONE SECOND OF FALSE-POSITIVE WINDOW. Case G in R4-F1's evidence (a command that runs the full cap and then exits 124) is irreducible for any elapsed heuristic. Case C (elapsed == cap-1) is NOT irreducible -- it is purchased entirely by the -1. So the only effect of the tolerance is to widen the set of self-inflicted 124s that are misreported as cap-caused. ALSO FOR THE RECORD, AN UNFLAGGED DEVIATION: R3-F1 specified the repair predicate as 'rc==124 AND elapsed>=cap'. The shipped predicate is '>= cap-1'. The deviation IS argued in the code -- on a premise that does not hold -- rather than flagged as a deviation from what the finding specified, so a reader comparing finding to fix sees agreement where there is a silent one-second widening. BINDING REPAIR, EITHER ARM: tighten to `-ge $GREEN_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S`, OR keep the -1 with a rationale that is TRUE (clock-step tolerance is a real one; `date +%s` truncation is not) and state explicitly what the tolerance costs in false positives.

findings.evidence: MEASURED under bash 3.2.57 against the verbatim-extracted shipped green_check_run, with a discriminating control. Log directory present but NOT writable (chmod 500), cap=3, command 'sleep 30': returns '1 watchdog false' AND RETURNS IMMEDIATELY. CONTROL, identical cap and command, writable directory: returns '124 watchdog true'. So the probe discriminates; it is not measuring a general failure to run. Mechanism: `bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1 &` fails its redirect, so the subshell exits 1 WITHOUT EVER RUNNING THE COMMAND; stderr carries two 'Permission denied' lines (from the `: > "$log"` truncate and from the job's own redirect) which cmd_green_check never sees. SELF-CORRECTION RECORDED: my first attempt at this probe ran under zsh, not bash ('set: can't change option: -m'), and returned empty output; I discarded that result and re-ran under bash before drawing any conclusion. The figures above are the bash run.
findings.description: A SUITE THAT NEVER RAN IS REPORTED AS A GENUINELY RED SUITE, WITH NO EVIDENCE AND timed_out=false. Reading the shipped code forward from the measured triple: :13663 `[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]` is false -> result='red', exit_code=1; :13695 `[ "$result" = "red" ] && [ -f "$log_path" ]` is false -> NO log tail, so the R2-F6 evidence block is empty in exactly the state where a reader most needs it. On a unit-bound task at --phase before that is the cannot_start_from_green refusal, whose own text instructs the agent 'Do NOT implement. Open the red baseline as its own task (bd_create_task, typed bug...)' -- for a baseline that does not exist, with no evidence to cite, and with the one field whose entire job is to explain why the run ended saying false. The cause is swallowed by `|| true` at :13653. THIS IS THE R3-F1 CLASS WITH A DIFFERENT TRIGGER: a measurement that did not happen, indistinguishable from one that ran and failed. Trigger is environmental (read-only checkout, sandboxed CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, ENOSPC), so I am rating MEDIUM for consistency with how R3-F3's same-consequence finding was rated -- it would be HIGH if the trigger were common. BINDING REPAIR: the correct idiom ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS SAME FILE at qa-gate.sh:8724 -- `if ! mkdir -p "$QA_TRACKING_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then` -- use it and emit a distinct error_key rather than inventing a new one. WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY: end-to-end envelope behaviour, because cmd_green_check calls add_comment and the store was quiet for this review; the green_check_run return is measured and the three downstream lines are read, and they are direct pass-throughs (:13658, :13713) with no branching on timed_out.

findings.evidence: The comment claims: 'This preserves the real exit code (124 when run_with_timeout's own timeout/gtimeout call fires the cap, per that binary's own convention; ANYTHING ELSE IS A GENUINE FAILURE) so downstream branches can DISTINGUISH TIMEOUT FROM FAILURE.' Read the branches it describes: :2580-2585 are `timeout "${secs}s" bash -c "$*"` and the gtimeout twin, with NEITHER a marker file NOR an elapsed check -- nothing but the binary's own return. The airtight reasoning run_with_timeout's header documents at :2543-2551 ('a killed process makes wait report 128+signal, never 124 on its own -- rc is forced to 124 by the caller, and ONLY via the marker-file check') applies ONLY to the `*)` watchdog branch, the sole branch that uses `wait`. Four consumers depend on the claim: :5291, :5307, :5320 and classify_test_failure:3732.
findings.description: THE IDENTICAL OVERCLAIM R3-F1 JUST RETIRED IN qa-gate.sh IS STILL LIVE IN THE STOP HOOK, for the real timeout/gtimeout binary case, in a file that has no timed_out equivalent. A test command that self-exits 124 is reported as 'Tests timed out after ${TEST_TIMEOUT_S}s'. THE IMPLEMENTER'S DECISION TO SCOPE THIS OUT WAS CORRECT AND I AM RULING IT SO: not named in any finding, different file, materially larger blast radius, and that file is under concurrent change (03tf.1, gsfd, j7kk). The gate DECISION is unaffected either way -- only the diagnosis. But a disclosure is not a follow-up task, and this needs one: it is now the only place in the codebase making a claim its sibling implementation has explicitly retracted, and green_check_run's own header cites run_with_timeout as its reference implementation, so the next reader inherits the wrong lesson from the file being cited as authority. Recorded here for the audit trail and FILED AS ITS OWN TASK per CONTRIBUTING.md; it is not a condition on approving fkm.7.

findings.evidence: CONFIRMED READ-ONLY, without invoking the writer, so nothing was posted to establish it. Reproduced the shipped selection against the live comment stream: three REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 first-lines exist (iteration=1 findings=[R1-F1:medium,R1-F2:low,R1-F3:low,R1-F4:low]; iteration=2 findings=[R2-F1:high..R2-F9:low]; iteration=3 findings=[R3-F1:high..R3-F6:low]). finding_id_in_latest_artifact selects the LAST in comment order via tail -1, and `grep -c 'R2-'` against that token returns 0. So resolve-finding and arbitrate (same guard) refuse any R1-*/R2-* id with finding_id_not_found and write nothing -- the implementer's report of this limitation is accurate and is NOT a mis-invocation. Checked the other half too: review-check.sh cmd_gate iterates $ART_FINDINGS, the findings of the SINGLE K3-selected artifact, not a union across artifacts.
findings.description: THE TWO HALVES ARE CONSISTENT, SO THIS IS NOT A GATE GAP TODAY: earlier rounds' findings stop gating at the same moment they stop being resolvable, and the intended discipline is that QA carries a still-open finding forward under a new R<n>-F<m> id -- which is exactly what happened on this task (R2-F2's residual became R3-F1 and R3-F2). I am ruling the implementer's report correct and the behaviour as-designed. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS REAL AND NOTHING MECHANICAL CATCHES IT: if a reviewer writes round N+1 and OMITS a still-open at-threshold finding, the gate silently forgets it, and the only trace is a RESOLVED record that never appears -- an absence, which is the hardest thing for an auditor to notice. Worth a task plus one line in qa.md stating that omission from a new artifact equals dismissal, so the choice is deliberate rather than accidental. LOW because it requires reviewer error and leaves an auditable absence, not because the consequence is small. FILED AS ITS OWN TASK; not a condition on approving fkm.7.
